topics.title: Properties, Constructors & Encapsulation
topics.summary: Build types whose public API protects invariants using access modifiers, validated setters, init-only values, and constructor requirements.

concepts.name: Access modifiers
concepts.explanation: public exposes a member broadly; private limits access to the containing type; protected and internal support inheritance/assembly boundaries.

concepts.name: Properties as behavior
concepts.explanation: A property can validate in its setter or compute in its getter. Do not expose mutable fields publicly when a property can preserve the type contract.

concepts.name: Initialization
concepts.explanation: Constructors, required members, and init accessors express what must be supplied when an object is created and what may change later.

topics.challenge: Create a class that validates a constructor argument and exposes at least one property with restricted modification.
topics.hint: Validate invalid state at the boundary, then make the valid value available through a property.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Inheritance, Interfaces & Polymorphism
topics.summary: Separate “is-a” inheritance from capability contracts and call behavior through base/interface types.

concepts.name: Inheritance
concepts.explanation: A class can derive from one base class. virtual members may be overridden by derived classes; base constructors and methods can be invoked with base.

concepts.name: Interfaces
concepts.explanation: Interfaces describe a contract without requiring a specific class hierarchy. A class can implement multiple interfaces.

concepts.name: Polymorphism
concepts.explanation: Code can depend on an interface/base type and receive different concrete implementations. This reduces coupling when the abstraction represents a real shared behavior.

topics.challenge: Create an interface with one property and one method, implement it in a class, and use the object through the interface type.
topics.hint: Write the interface contract first, then make the class provide every required member.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Collections, Dictionaries & Enumeration
topics.summary: Choose arrays, List<T>, Dictionary<TKey,TValue>, HashSet<T>, queues, and stacks based on access and uniqueness needs.

concepts.name: Dictionary
concepts.explanation: Dictionary<TKey,TValue> maps unique keys to values and provides fast lookup by key in typical cases.

concepts.name: HashSet
concepts.explanation: HashSet<T> stores unique values and supports set operations such as union, intersection, and membership tests.

concepts.name: Enumeration
concepts.explanation: foreach works with the enumeration pattern/IEnumerable<T>. Avoid modifying many collections structurally while enumerating them unless the API documents it as safe.

topics.challenge: Create a Dictionary<string,int> and a HashSet<string>, add values, and perform one lookup/membership check.
topics.hint: A dictionary uses two generic type arguments: one for keys and one for values.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Exceptions & Defensive Error Handling
topics.summary: Represent exceptional failures with exceptions, preserve useful context, and distinguish validation from broad catch-all handling.

concepts.name: Throwing
concepts.explanation: Throw exceptions when a method cannot satisfy its contract. Standard exception types such as ArgumentException and InvalidOperationException communicate common failure categories.

concepts.name: try/catch/finally
concepts.explanation: Catch only where you can recover, translate, log, or add useful context. finally is for cleanup that must occur whether the operation succeeds or fails.

concepts.name: Do not hide failures
concepts.explanation: An empty catch block destroys evidence. Preserve the original exception when wrapping it, and avoid using exceptions as routine branch logic.

topics.challenge: Write a method that throws a meaningful exception for invalid input and a caller that handles it with try/catch.
topics.hint: Use a specific exception inside the method. The caller decides whether it can recover or report the error.

references.title: Microsoft Learn — A tour of C#

topics.title: Files, using & Resource Lifetime
topics.summary: Read/write local files and ensure disposable resources are released even when an operation fails.

concepts.name: File helpers
concepts.explanation: File.ReadAllText/WriteAllText and async variants cover small straightforward file operations without manual stream management.

concepts.name: IDisposable
concepts.explanation: Some resources own operating-system or unmanaged handles. IDisposable provides deterministic cleanup through Dispose.

concepts.name: using
concepts.explanation: using statements/declarations call Dispose automatically at scope exit, including exceptional paths. await using does the same for IAsyncDisposable.

topics.challenge: Write text to a local file, read it back, and use at least one using declaration with a disposable file/stream object.
topics.hint: Use File helpers for the simple operation and a using declaration when you create a disposable stream directly.
